note: Pose measurements taken off the side-on product shot of a loaded dumbbell (camera on the handle's midline). These are what the camera constants in src/components/weight/three/scale.ts are derived from. Pixel figures come from the 586x374 source; ratios are what actually carry over.
method: Threshold dark metal against the pale backdrop, take the per-column vertical extent, then read the innermost plate's face ellipse off the inner silhouette. The ellipse is sampled where sqrt(1 - ((y-cy)/b)^2) = 0.5, i.e. at y = cy +/- 0.866b.

adopted.faceEllipseNote: The first pass derived distance from the inner face at 0.29. On a thick urethane puck the outer face then opened to ~0.48, so each head read as a disc on a diagonal. Distance is now set from the outer face of the heaviest head (DB_INNER_FACE_X + max thickness) so that face foreshortens to 0.20 — side-on, same language as the loaded bar. The inner face falls out at ~0.11.

deviations.reference: plate-loaded stack, four discs per side, spinlock collars
deviations.why: The gym reference for the model is a circular-head urethane dumbbell. The photo is used only as the camera pose — midline, slight elevation, faces reading as ellipses — the same language as the loaded bar.
A circular-head bell is a short handle with two fat pucks. Keeping real urethane proportions matters more than matching a long plate-loaded handle.
